senses.d: An instrument for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a tool, or an opportunity or pretext.
ex: They overturned him to all his interests by the sure but fatal handle of his own good nature.
Nothing can be more reprehensible, or wicked, than to make Christian Missions a handle for political expansion.

senses.d: The gross amount of wagering within a given period of time or for a given event at one of more establishments.
ex: The daily handle of a Las Vegas casino is typically millions of dollars.

senses.d: The tactile qualities of a fabric, e.g., softness, firmness, elasticity, fineness, resilience, and other qualities perceived by touch.
A name or nickname, especially as an identifier over the radio or Internet.
ex: We sat together at the restaurant and asked him about his handle (CB name).
"I don't actually know his birth name. He just uses his handle."

senses.d: A title attached to one's name, such as Doctor or Colonel.
ex: The successful businessman was knighted and acquired a handle to his name.

senses.d: A reference to an object or structure that can be stored in a variable.
ex: This article describes how to find the module name from the window handle.

senses.d: A traditional dimpled glass with a handle, for serving a pint of beer.
A 10 fluid ounce (285 mL) glass of beer.
ex: A shudder passes over him and he orders another handle of beer.
When ordering a beer, you'll get either a handle (mug) or a one-liter jug (pitcher).

senses.d: A half-gallon (1.75-liter) bottle of alcohol.
To touch; to feel or hold with the hand(s).
ex: Happy, ye leaves! when as those lilly hands [...] Shall handle you.
Handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh.

senses.d: To accustom to the hand; to take care of with the hands.
ex: The hardness of the winters forces the breeders to house and handle their colts for at least six months every year.

senses.d: To manage, use, or wield with the hands.
ex: That fellow handles his bow like a crowkeeper
Light on his feet for a big man, he handled the rifle like a pistol.

senses.d: To manage, control, or direct.
ex: You shall see how I'll handle her
“You also handle the accounts for Julie Wojakowski, what about her? Any recent deposits in that amount?”

senses.d: To treat, to deal with (in a specified way).
ex: she handled the news with grace
the Persians handled the French ambassador shamefully

senses.d: To deal with (a subject, argument, topic, or theme) in speaking, in writing, or in art.
ex: We will handle what persons are apt to envy others...

senses.d: To receive and transfer; to have pass through one's hands; hence, to buy and sell.
ex: a merchant handles a variety of goods, or a large stock

senses.d: To be concerned with; to be an expert in.
ex: They that handle the law knew me not

senses.d: To put up with; to endure (and continue to function).
ex: I can't handle this hot weather.
For example, a program that loads data from a file needs to handle the case where that file is not found.

senses.d: To use the hands.
ex: They [idols made of gold and silver] have hands, but they handle not
